newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: OLYMPICS-SYDNEY 2000 GETS NEW GAMES CHIEF.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-SYDNEY 2000 GETS NEW GAMES CHIEF.

text.p: Sydney's 2000 Olympics organising committee appointed a former prime ministerial adviser as chief executive on Thursday in its third major management upheaval in a year.
Sandy Hollway, a career bureaucrat who worked in the office of former Labor prime minister Bob Hawke, replaced Mal Hemmerling, whose resignation was accepted earlier on Thursday.

Hemmerling, who held the post since 1995 after running the Australian Formula One Grand Prix in Adelaide for 10 years, told reporters at a hastily-arranged news conference that he had resigned to pursue other career interests.
The Sydney Olympic Committee for the Olympic Games (SOCOG) has lost a host of board members over the past two years. Several senior executives have also left.

Businessman John Iliffe resigned as SOCOG president last September, only six months after his predecessor Gary Pemberton stepped down from the job. Iliffe was replaced by regional politician Michael Knight.
Hollway joined SOCOG in December as deputy chief executive.
